hero.subtitle: Five days moving from vermillion torii gates to bamboo groves to lantern-lit lanes — paced for two travelers who want culture and food without the rush.

image.alt: Misty hillside temple grounds at dawn

overview.label: Route Strategy
overview.value: Single base in central Kyoto; radiate outward to Arashiyama and the northern temples, return each night.

overview.label: Weather
overview.value: Mild, 15–22°C with occasional rain — pack a compact umbrella.

overview.label: Currency
overview.value: Japanese Yen (¥). Cash still rules at small shrines and food stalls.

overview.label: Transportation
overview.value: JR trains for day trips, city buses and subway within Kyoto, walking through old districts.

overview.label: Travel Style
overview.value: Culture-forward with deliberate food stops — temples in the morning light, markets by dusk.

overview.label: Key Highlights
overview.value: Fushimi Inari at sunrise, Arashiyama bamboo grove, Kinkaku-ji, Nishiki Market, Gion at night.

days.title: Vermillion Gates & Old Kyoto Dusk

coverImage.alt: Rows of red torii gates climbing a wooded hillside

beats.text: Breakfast at a Kyoto Station café before the crowds arrive.
Fushimi Inari Shrine — climb the early torii gate paths while the light is still soft.
Inari-zushi and grilled skewers from the stalls at the shrine's base.
Tofuku-ji Temple — quiet Zen gardens a short train ride from Fushimi.
% Arabica Kyoto for a slow coffee and a breather.
Wander Gion's lantern-lit lanes; watch for geiko heading to evening appointments.
Kaiseki-style multi-course dinner at a small Gion restaurant.

days.tip: Arrive at Fushimi Inari before 9am; by mid-morning the lower gates are shoulder to shoulder.

days.title: Bamboo, River, and Riverside Quiet

coverImage.alt: Tall bamboo grove with light filtering through

beats.text: Early JR train to Arashiyama to catch the bamboo grove before tour groups.
Walk the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, then continue to Tenryu-ji Temple's garden.
Yudofu (hot tofu) set meal at a temple-adjacent restaurant.
Togetsukyo Bridge and the riverside path; rent a rowboat if the weather holds.
Riverside café with views back toward the hills.
Return to central Kyoto; browse Teramachi covered shopping street.
Izakaya dinner — small plates and local sake near Pontocho.

days.tip: Skip the Monkey Park if short on time; the bamboo grove and Tenryu-ji alone fill a satisfying morning.

hotels.title: Ryokan Suiran, Arashiyama
hotels.text: A riverside luxury ryokan with private onsen baths and kaiseki breakfast included.

hotels.title: Hotel Granvia Kyoto
hotels.text: Directly above Kyoto Station — best pick for minimizing transit time on arrival and departure days.

hotels.title: Gion Nanba
hotels.text: Small boutique ryokan tucked in a quiet Gion side street, three minutes from the main lantern-lit lane.

restaurants.title: Omen Nishiki
restaurants.text: Handmade udon in a warm dashi broth with a plate of seasonal vegetables to dip.

restaurants.title: Gion Karyo
restaurants.text: Multi-course kaiseki built around whatever is best at the market that morning.

restaurants.title: Kagizen Yoshifusa
restaurants.text: 150-year-old confectioner known for kuzukiri (arrowroot noodles) in cold syrup.

transport.title: Airport transfer
transport.text: Haruka Express from Kansai Airport to Kyoto Station, roughly 75 minutes.

transport.title: Local transport
transport.text: City buses and subway; a day pass pays off on temple-heavy days.

transport.title: Walking advice
transport.text: Higashiyama and Arashiyama are best explored on foot — plan for uneven stone paths.

transport.title: Money-saving tip
transport.text: An ICOCA IC card covers buses, subway, and konbini purchases in one tap.

budget.note: Biggest expenses are accommodation and kaiseki dining. Saving tip: eat one casual noodle or market meal per day to offset a splurge dinner. Figures converted at approx. ₹0.586/¥1 (Jul 2026); actual payments in Japan are made in yen.

packing.title: Clothing
packing.text: Layers for 15–22°C days; modest attire for temple visits.

packing.title: Weather essentials
packing.text: Compact umbrella and a light rain shell for spring showers.

packing.title: Walking / transport
packing.text: Broken-in walking shoes with grip for stone-paved slopes.

packing.title: Electronics
packing.text: Universal plug adapter (Type A) and a power bank for full sightseeing days.

packing.title: Documents
packing.text: Passport, travel insurance details, and printed hotel confirmations.

packing.title: Trip-specific
packing.text: A small tote for market and tea purchases along the way.

tips.text: Kyoto is very safe; ordinary city awareness after dark is sufficient.
Bow lightly at shrine entrances; keep voices low inside temple grounds.
IC cards and major credit cards work in most places; carry cash for small stalls.
The upper torii tunnels at Fushimi Inari just after sunrise.
Otagi Nenbutsu-ji — a quiet hillside temple with 1,200 individually carved stone statues, well past the Arashiyama crowds.
